title: Dedicated/Private: per-customer profile pin + override guardrails (audit + rollback)
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Goal
- Allow Dedicated and Private customers to pin a specific hardware tuning profile (profile_version + optional profile_id) per deployment/customer, with safety guardrails.
- Ensure changes are auditable, reversible, and safe-by-default.

Context
- Hosted will roll out profile pack defaults via canary + kill-switch. Dedicated/Private require explicit customer-level control and rollback to avoid surprises and to support regulated change management.
- Customers have asked for deterministic performance behavior and the ability to “stay on known-good” during POCs and production incidents.

Scope
1) Override surface area
- Dedicated: support per-customer (tenant) override stored in control-plane config, propagated to runtime via existing config distribution.
- Private: support Helm values / installer config override (values.yaml) with equivalent schema + validation.
- Overrides supported:
  - Pin `profile_version` (required for any override)
  - Optional pin `profile_id` (if multiple profiles exist per SKU within a version)
  - Optional `selection_mode=locked` to disable auto-upgrades when new default versions ship.

2) Guardrails (hard blocks)
- Compatibility gate: refuse override if detected (sku, driver, cuda, mig_mode) not compatible with the pinned profile pack.
- Safety gate: refuse override if profile requires knobs that violate runtime “safe defaults” (e.g., memory headroom below minimum, concurrency above max for SKU).
- Refuse “unknown version”: runtime must not accept arbitrary strings; only versions present in the shipped pack artifact or explicitly allowlisted.

3) Auditability
- All override changes must be recorded with:
  - who (actor: user/service), when, where (env/region), what (previous -> new value), and why (required change reason field).
  - correlation to rollout/incident ticket when applicable.
- Dedicated: emit an audit log event from control plane + mirror a structured runtime startup log including the effective override source.
- Private: emit a structured “config override detected” event to runtime logs and /health debug fields.

4) Safe rollback
- Provide a single action to revert to fleet default selection:
  - Dedicated: remove override in control-plane (revert to “inherit default”), with propagation confirmation.
  - Private: set override fields to empty and redeploy.
- Runtime behavior: on rollback, selection logic must be deterministic and identical to non-overridden customers.
- Include a guard against “partial state”: if model reload happens during propagation, runtime must not mix versions across loaded models.

Implementation notes
- Precedence (highest -> lowest):
  1) Explicit customer pin (Dedicated control-plane / Private helm values)
  2) Fleet default version for deployment mode
  3) Runtime built-in fallback defaults (only for emergency if pack artifact missing)
- Logging: at runtime startup and at model load, log effective `profile_version`, `profile_id`, detected sku, and `override_source` (fleet_default | customer_pin | emergency_fallback).

Acceptance criteria
- Dedicated:
  - Control-plane API supports setting/clearing per-customer profile pin.
  - Override changes create an audit log record with required reason.
  - Runtime reports active profile pin via /health and debug endpoint.
- Private:
  - Helm chart exposes override fields with docs and validation failure modes.
  - Installer warns on unsupported driver/CUDA for pinned version.
- Guardrails:
  - Invalid pins are rejected with actionable error messages (including detected hw and required baseline).
  - Unsafe pins cannot be forced without an explicit break-glass mechanism (separate approval path; out of scope to implement now, but error message should direct to SRE).
- Tests:
  - Unit tests for precedence + compatibility checks.
  - Integration test that verifies rollback returns to fleet default and does not leave stale profile state across model reload.

Out of scope (explicit)
- UI/Console configuration workflow for setting overrides (tracked separately; DES-214 covers visibility UX).
- Break-glass bypass mechanism (we only block + instruct).

Links
- Epic: ENG-4921 (Hardware tuning profiles pack)
- Related implementation PR (runtime config pin + guardrails + audit hook): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/24944
- Related: selection logic https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/24881
- Related: /health profile version https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/25014
- Private Helm exposure: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-helm-charts/pull/144
- Private installer compatibility warning: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-private-installer/pull/602

Risks / notes
- Cardinality: ensure profile_id/profile_version tags do not explode in metrics (only a small set of versions should be active). Coordinate with Allison/Caleb on ingestion limits.
- Change management: Dedicated customers may require scheduled windows; Product to align on messaging and recommended pinning strategy.

Rollout plan (Dedicated)
- Phase 1: feature available but restricted to internal canary tenants (SRE approval required).
- Phase 2: allow for early-access customers with support playbook and rollback steps.
- Phase 3: general availability once SLO guardrails and dashboards are validated.
comments: 2026-02-06 (Benji Okafor): Implemented override precedence + validation plumbing in runtime config. Added structured startup log fields `override_source` and `pinned_profile_version`. Pending: ensure audit log includes required “reason” and is enforced at API layer. PR: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/24944

2026-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): Please add a clear rollback runbook snippet for on-call: exact API call to clear override + how to verify propagation (health/debug endpoint). Also want an explicit metric panel for “override adoption” by tenant to spot accidental pins.

2026-02-12 (Lauren Bishop): For Dedicated, we should avoid exposing knob-level overrides in customer-facing language. Pinning version is OK; make sure errors instruct to contact support rather than suggesting manual knob edits.

2026-02-14 (Irene Choi): Compatibility checks need to include MIG mode and driver/CUDA baselines. We have region variance right now; please ensure error text prints detected driver and the required minimum for the pinned version.

2026-02-18 (Rafael Mendes): Confirm kill-switch semantics: clearing override should be enough; no separate restart required beyond config propagation. Also please make sure audit event includes correlation id so we can tie to incident threads.
